- **self**: Human baselines and control words for tic detection (7/2)

## How it works

- [statement] Kobak et al. build a counterfactual baseline by linear extrapolation from earlier years (q = p_{Y-2} + 2*max{p_{Y-2}-p_{Y-3},0}) and deliberately exclude 2023 because it may already be LLM-affected. (medium confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2406.07016 · keywords: Human baselines and control words for tic detection · also: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2510.15061

## Measurements and reference values

- [statement] Control by word class: authors hand-annotated 900 excess words from 2013-2024 as content (about 51%) or style (about 45%); Covid-era excess was mostly content nouns, 2024 excess mostly style verbs and adjectives, which separates topical drift from LLM tics. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2406.07016 · keywords: Human baselines and control words for tic detection

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Excess-word counts are only a lower bound on LLM use, and cannot distinguish LLM use from authors independently adopting LLM-preferred vocabulary. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2406.07016 · keywords: Human baselines and control words for tic detection

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Excess words are flagged using two metrics, frequency gap and frequency ratio; thresholds were chosen so most pre-Covid years fall well below them, giving conservative estimates. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2406.07016 · keywords: Human baselines and control words for tic detection
- [statement] Human baselines for model-output tic detection can be built from pre-2022 corpora (wordfreq for single words; Reddit creative writing and Project Gutenberg for n-grams in Antislop), with overuse expressed as a ratio of model frequency to baseline frequency. (medium confidence) — https://arxiv.org/pdf/2510.15061 · keywords: Human baselines and control words for tic detection · also: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2412.11385
- [statement] Post-2021 web text is contaminated by generative-AI output, so frequency resources built from it no longer measure human language; wordfreq's maintainer stopped updating it for this reason, forcing baselines to pre-2022 archives. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2024-09-15) — https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=41578483 · keywords: Human baselines and control words for tic detection · also: https://arxiv.org/html/2406.07016
- [statement] Confound check: the hypothesis that 'delve' reflects Nigerian English annotators was not supported by International Corpus of English data (small corpus); RLHF-based Llama experiments fit better as the source of overrepresentation. (medium confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2412.11385v1 · keywords: Human baselines and control words for tic detection · also: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2412.11385
